title: Merged work leaves no worktrees or branches behind, and a wrapping session offers the fast cleanup
why: Your idea, Oct 25: when a session thinks its work is wrapped, it should offer you a faster worktree cleanup than the scheduled ones.
note: Checked at claude-settings f463787. Cleanup today runs on its own at four points (decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed): each agent end removes a finished agent's tree after 30 idle minutes; each session end and the daily job remove a merged tree idle 1 hour, an agent tree idle 4 hours, a pushed unmerged tree idle 24 hours. A dirty or unpushed tree is never removed. The fast path already exists: janitor/sweep.py --attended (a person's run, skips the merged and 1-hour idle keeps) and --fast (only trees whose branch is already in main, no fetch); preview by default, --confirm to remove. Gap: no rule tells a session to offer it, so you never hear of it. Unknown: how many worktrees pile up today on the Mac and Windows (count .claude/worktrees per repo and read state/janitor-runs.jsonl). Advisor pick, not ruled: one sentence in the reports rule's home: when a session's last PR has merged and no lane is open, its final report offers the cleanup as one command you can run (c28 pattern): sweep.py --root <repo> --attended --fast, preview then --confirm. No hook, no new code. Your word, Oct 25: you were checking whether it existed; goal 3 already went out without it, so it waits for a later batch. Mac session report, Oct 25 (ios-ship and guard-cull lanes): after both PRs merged, their worktrees and local branches stayed. Causes it found: the merge tool deletes the remote branch, keeps a local branch that a worktree has checked out, and never removes worktrees; the Agent tool keeps a subagent's worktree when it holds commits and locks it with the host session's pid, and the sweep frees such a lock only when that pid is dead, so the tree waits until the session ends. Friction seen: unlock and remove in one command is refused (the guard reads the lock first); a stale tree with only deletions had to be committed on a throwaway branch (discard-a4f61ca) to pass the guard, and that branch then could not be deleted (only copy), so the guard's remedy left junk for you to delete by hand. Advisor pick, Oct 25, not ruled: after a merge, the merge tool runs the sweep's --fast removal for that one branch's clean worktree, and the sweep treats a lock held by the calling session's own pid on a finished agent's merged, clean tree as freeable. Unknown: whether the merge tool's 'never removes worktrees' has a recorded reason (read decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed first). The Mac now holds only main and one pin (2026afc4), per your word that claude-settings building happens on Windows.
